description: We are a team of aspiring engineers driven by curiosity, creativity, and a passion for innovation. United by a shared dream, we aim to explore new possibilities and turn ideas into reality.
summary:
MISSION CONTROL is an interactive, browser-based 3D space exploration and aerospace engineering simulator that allows users to experience the complete lifecycle of an interplanetary space mission.

The application enables users to design and assemble modular spacecraft, configure propulsion and power systems, evaluate engineering parameters, perform launch simulations, navigate orbital environments and conduct planetary investigations across four campaigns: Mars, the Moon, asteroid Bennu and Europa.

It addresses the challenge of making complex aerospace engineering and planetary science concepts more accessible through interactive visualization and game-based learning. By combining simplified engineering models, scientific reference information and immersive 3D environments, users can understand how spacecraft design decisions influence mission performance and survival.

MISSION CONTROL aims to bridge the gap between theoretical aerospace education and practical interactive experimentation, making space exploration more engaging and accessible without requiring expensive physical equipment or professional simulation infrastructure.
details:
MISSION CONTROL integrates several engineering and simulation modules to provide an interactive spacecraft operations experience.

Core Functionalities

- Spacecraft Assembly: Modular selection of structural buses, propulsion systems, solar arrays, batteries, thermal management, communication equipment, navigation systems and scientific payloads.

- Engineering Validation: Evaluation of spacecraft mass, available Delta-V, power generation, electrical consumption, thermal conditions and communication link budgets.

- Launch Operations: Pre-launch system checks, countdown sequences, simulated multi-stage launch and orbital deployment.

- Orbital Navigation: Third-person spacecraft control with simulated propulsion, attitude control and navigation.

- Scientific Exploration: Mission-specific investigations using simulated scientific instruments.

- Mission Survival: Dynamic emergency scenarios involving power management, thermal regulation, propulsion and spacecraft control.

Benefits

- Encourages practical understanding of spacecraft engineering.

- Demonstrates how engineering decisions influence mission performance.

- Develops technical problem-solving and decision-making skills.

- Provides an accessible environment for aerospace experimentation without physical prototypes or specialized simulation infrastructure.

Intended Impact

The project aims to encourage interest in aerospace engineering, spacecraft systems and planetary science. It promotes interdisciplinary learning, engineering-based decision-making and a deeper understanding of the technical challenges associated with space missions.

Technology Stack

- Programming Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5 and CSS.

- Frameworks and Libraries: React 18, Three.js, Zustand, Tailwind CSS and Lucide React.

- Development Tools: Google Antigravity, Gemini, Vite, Node.js and npm.

- Web Technologies: WebGL, Web Audio API and LocalStorage.

- Deployment: GitHub for source code management and Vercel for hosting.

- Hardware: No dedicated physical hardware is required. The application runs on compatible computers with a modern web browser and WebGL support.

Creative Approach

The project combines spacecraft engineering with interactive simulation and game-based exploration. Engineering dashboards, modular component selection, orbital operations and dynamic survival scenarios allow users to experience the consequences of technical decisions rather than simply study theoretical concepts.

Design Considerations

- Energy Efficiency: Incorporates spacecraft power generation, electrical consumption and variations in solar irradiance.

- Accessibility: Browser-based operation eliminates specialized installation and dedicated laboratory requirements.

- Cost: Avoids expensive physical prototypes and professional simulation infrastructure.

- Environmental Considerations: Encourages virtual experimentation and introduces the importance of energy efficiency, thermal management and resource optimization in spacecraft systems.
